---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Asset-Scaled Profit Payoff Balance Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che,MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oibdp,dp),at),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(oibdp,1),LAG(at,1)),1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash-backed firms outperform when post-depreciation profitability is strong and operating profit is increasing relative to the existing asset base.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Scaling incremental operating profit by lagged assets tests whether the physical-payoff result reflects broad capital productivity rather than an unusually small depreciation denominator. The current post-depreciation return remains binding, so profit growth from an unproductive base cannot define the long portfolio.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Organizational-Payoff Balance Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che,MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oiadp,at),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(oiadp,1),LAG(xsga,1)),1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash-backed firms outperform when they are currently profitable and prior organizational spending is producing incremental operating income.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Operating-income improvement per dollar of lagged SG&A measures realized payoff from the organizational cost base rather than rewarding expense contraction. Using the same liquidity valuation channel as the physical-capital winner provides an informative comparison of whether tangible or organizational investment productivity strengthens cash value.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: R&D-Budgeted Incremental Franchise
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(che,TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt)),3)),MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oiadp,COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt))),ADD(at,TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt)),3))),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(oiadp,COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt))),1),LAG(ADD(at,TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt)),3)),1)),1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with liquidity exceeding a recent R&D budget outperform when intangible-inclusive profitability is high and adjusted operating profit is increasing relative to prior productive capital.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The valuation leg measures conservatively budgeted innovation liquidity, while the two quality channels separately require a high return level and a strong incremental return on tangible plus recent R&D capital. This tests an R&D-capital payoff mechanism without relying on a small R&D-only denominator.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Enterprise-Cash Post-Depreciation Payoff
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf,xint),ADD(MUL(prcc_f,csho),SUB(ADD(dltt,dlc),che))),1)),MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oibdp,dp),at),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(oibdp,dp),1),LAG(dp,1)),1))))
HYPOTHESIS: High pre-interest cash-flow-to-enterprise-value firms outperform when post-depreciation profitability is strong and improving relative to the depreciable asset base.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Using the change in profit after depreciation aligns the incremental-payoff measure with the current post-depreciation return rather than mixing pre- and post-depreciation accounting concepts. The construction tests whether productive physical capital validates enterprise cash cheapness rather than balance-sheet cash backing alone.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Maintenance-Capacity Balance Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che,MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oibdp,dp),at),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oancf,dp),1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash-backed firms outperform when they combine strong post-depreciation profitability with operating cash flow sufficient to cover asset consumption.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Operating cash flow relative to depreciation measures the capacity to replenish the productive asset base without consuming balance-sheet liquidity. Requiring strong post-depreciation ROA prevents mechanically high coverage at firms with low depreciation but weak operations from qualifying.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Pretax-Conversion Balance Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che,MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(pi,at),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(pi,ADD(ABS(pi),ABS(oibdp))),1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash-backed firms outperform when pretax profitability is strong and operating earnings convert efficiently into pretax income.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Pretax ROA establishes the level of profitability, while pretax income divided by the combined magnitude of pretax and operating cash earnings provides a bounded conversion measure. Making both dimensions binding filters cash-rich firms whose operating profits are largely absorbed before reaching equity-relevant pretax earnings.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---CRITIQUE Asset-Scaled Profit Payoff Balance Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a single-denominator swap (lag dp → lag at) on the archive's best performer, Physical-Capital Payoff Balance Value, and the resulting Δoibdp/lag(at) leg is little more than the well-known profitability-change signal, so it is a cosmetic robustness variant rather than a new mechanism.

---CRITIQUE Organizational-Payoff Balance Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The expression simply grafts the valuation leg of the archived Cash-Backed/Physical-Capital family (che/mktcap) onto the quality leg of the archived SG&A-Payoff Cash Value, a pure recombination of two already-evaluated signals whose incremental information over che/mktcap × ROA is likely minimal.

---CRITIQUE R&D-Budgeted Incremental Franchise---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: It takes the valuation leg of the archived R&D-Budgeted Liquidity Franchise and the MIN(level, DELTA) intangible-ROA quality leg of the archived Liquidity-Backed Intangible Productivity, producing a highly parameterized hybrid of two already-tested signals with no genuinely new economic channel.

---CRITIQUE Enterprise-Cash Post-Depreciation Payoff---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The internal-consistency fix (differencing post-depreciation rather than pre-depreciation profit) is a real accounting alignment improvement, and pairing it with the enterprise-level cash yield rather than balance-sheet cash tests whether the payoff mechanism survives a genuinely different valuation channel, though it remains a close relative of the archived winner.

---CRITIQUE Maintenance-Capacity Balance Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This differs from the archived Cash-Burn-Protected Balance Value only by rescaling the cash-flow leg from at to dp, a mechanical denominator change that also reintroduces the low-depreciation distortion the proposal's own reasoning claims to guard against.

---CRITIQUE Pretax-Conversion Balance Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The conversion ratio pi/(|pi|+|oibdp|) is internally inconsistent with the stated hypothesis — it rewards pretax income being large relative to operating earnings, which flags non-operating gains and low depreciation/interest intensity as "efficient conversion" — and the ABS construction makes the measure non-monotone for loss firms while being largely collinear with the pi/at level leg.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Gross-to-Pretax Funnel Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(oancf,3),MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt,cogs),at),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(pi,SUB(revt,cogs)),1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms priced cheaply relative to cumulative cash generation outperform when they produce substantial gross profit and retain a large portion of it through the pretax-income line.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Gross profit to assets measures the size of the operating profit pool, while pretax income to gross profit measures leakage from overhead, depreciation, financing, and other items. Making the weaker channel binding creates a profit-funnel mechanism rather than another incremental-profit scaling variant of the physical-capital winner.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Organizational Profit Surprise Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(oiadp,1),MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oiadp,xsga),1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms priced cheaply relative to newly created operating income outperform when their existing organizational spending base is productive.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: The valuation leg measures incremental operating profit relative to market value rather than reusing cash holdings. Operating income per dollar of SG&A separately requires the new profit to arise within an efficient organizational cost structure, distinguishing scalable improvement from growth purchased through excessive overhead.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Innovation Profit Surprise Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(oiadp,COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt))),1),MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oiadp,COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt))),ADD(at,TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd,SUB(revt,revt)),3))),1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms priced cheaply relative to growth in R&D-adjusted operating profit outperform when their tangible-plus-intangible capital is currently productive.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: The value leg prices the year-over-year increase in operating profit after reversing R&D expensing, eliminating the prior liquidity-budget construction. The separate total-capital return requires that incremental adjusted profit be supported by a productive franchise rather than a rebound from a low base.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Maintenance-Adjusted Cash Franchise
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf,dp),MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oibdp,dp),at),1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with high cash yield after an allowance for asset consumption outperform when post-depreciation operating profitability is strong.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: Subtracting depreciation from operating cash flow creates a conservative maintenance-adjusted valuation flow without dividing by a potentially tiny depreciation amount. Post-depreciation ROA independently confirms that the inexpensive residual cash flow comes from productive operations rather than deferred asset replacement.

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: EBIT-to-Pretax Integrity Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ni,MUL(prcc_f,csho)),1)),IND_RANK(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(pi,at),ABS(RATIO(SUB(SUB(oibdp,dp),pi),at))),1)))
HYPOTHESIS: High net-income-yield firms outperform when pretax profitability is strong and closely supported by operating income after depreciation.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Comparing pretax income with post-depreciation operating profit removes the mechanical depreciation mismatch in the prior conversion measure. The absolute gap penalty caps the benefit of non-operating gains and penalizes financing or non-operating leakage, while negative pretax profitability naturally receives a low score.
